observations: PlayStation 4 Slim console with a 'Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War' decorative wrap.
A boxed white DualShock 4 controller with red custom patterns on the touchpad and grips.
TV screen shows the PS4 dashboard with a 'Gold Hen' icon, which indicates the console is jailbroken.
Game icons visible on screen include a modded 'EA Sports FC 26' (a non-existent title, likely a modded older version), GTA V, Ghost of Tsushima, and God of War.
The console is connected to a TCL television.
A second, blue controller is partially visible on a shelf below the console.

claims.evidence: The 'Gold Hen' icon in photo 1 and 2 confirms the console is running a jailbreak-compatible low firmware version.
The console has a Call of Duty themed skin visible in photo 0.
While game icons are visible in photo 1, they are not shown launching or playing; 'FC 26' is a known modded title name.

risks.risk: Specific firmware version (e.g., 9.00 vs 11.00) significantly affects value.
risks.proof: Screenshot of Settings > System > System Information.

risks.risk: The controller may be a high-quality clone rather than original Sony hardware.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the rear label and the charging port.

risks.risk: The optical disc drive may be faulty.
risks.proof: Video of a disc being inserted, recognized, and launched.

proof_requests: Photo of the System Information screen showing the exact firmware version.
Photo of the Storage screen showing the hard drive capacity.
Video of one of the installed games being launched and played.
Photo of the model number sticker on the back or bottom of the console.
response.reason: The item is clearly a PlayStation 4 Slim. The presence of the Gold Hen icon confirms it is a jailbroken unit, which allows for pricing based on that specific hardware state, even if the exact storage and firmware version are not yet proven.
